name: H&R Block, Inc.
reason: Cash-generative, buyback-driven tax preparer (10y ROIC 28%, shares -4.9%/yr) but EPS is at its 10y peak (1.0x) with EBIT margin in the 91st percentile on 2.7%/yr revenue growth, and AI-driven/free DIY filing is a credible disintermediation threat to assisted tax prep within 5 years.

name: Cabot Corporation
reason: Carbon black is a commodity chemical tied to tyre/auto volumes and feedstock pricing; EPS is 1.0x its 10y max with EBIT margin at a 10y high (17.0% vs 12.7% avg, 100th pctile) and consensus FY1 EPS -12%, i.e. at a cyclical peak.

name: PulteGroup, Inc.
reason: Well-run, net-cash homebuilder (ND/EBITDA 0.09x, shares -5.7%/yr) but earnings are set by housing/mortgage-rate cycles no one can forecast; EPS already fell 24% in 2025 from a 21.7% peak margin and consensus FY1 is -9.6%.

name: Euronet Worldwide, Inc.
reason: Mix of ATM networks, prepaid epay and Ria money transfer with 9/10 years of >=7% EPS growth, but adjusted EPS runs 67% above GAAP, the 5.6x NTM P/E signals market doubts on digital disintermediation of cash/remittance and new US remittance tax, and the segment mix is hard to forecast 10 years out.

name: Selective Insurance Group, Inc.
reason: Long-record regional commercial P&C underwriter with 10.6% 10y EPS CAGR and minimal acquisitions, but the 2024 casualty reserve charge (EPS -44.5%) and social-inflation exposure make loss-cost trends and underwriting discipline hard to forecast with confidence.

name: Hawaiian Electric Industries, Inc.
reason: Maui wildfire litigation settlement (2024 EBIT margin -53%) has crushed earnings (EPS 0.38x 10y max, 10y EPS CAGR -6.3%), diluted shareholders (+5%/yr shares) and left ND/EBITDA ~4.0x in a single-island regulated utility with ongoing wildfire liability.

name: Westamerica Bancorporation
reason: Exceptionally low-cost-deposit, conservatively underwritten California bank, but earnings are driven by rates on a shrinking deposit base (EPS 0.75x the 2023 rate-driven peak, rev CAGR 4.0%, consensus FY2-FY3 4-7%), so there is no plausible route to >=7%/yr EPS growth.

name: International Paper Company
reason: Containerboard/pulp is a commodity business with 10y ROIC 4.8%, EPS falling from 5.04 (2018) to -0.08 (2025), ND/EBITDA 3.6x and a transforming DS Smith acquisition plus share issuance (+1.9%/yr).

name: Brinker International Incorporated
reason: Chili's value-menu turnaround has taken EPS from 2.83 (FY23) to 10.74 (FY26), 1.0x the 10y max with EBIT margin at a 10y high (10.8% vs 7.3% avg); a casual-dining traffic surge at peak margins is not forecastable 5-10 years out.

name: Tennant Company
reason: Ordinary cleaning-equipment maker with 6.3% 10y EPS CAGR, 10y ROIC 7.8%, acquisition spend 85% of FCF, EBIT margin 6.1% (18th pctile) and adjusted EPS 40% above GAAP; no specialness.

name: Gap, Inc.
reason: Fashion-driven apparel retailer with negative 10y EPS CAGR (-1.3%), flat revenue (-0.3%/yr), two loss years since 2020 and only 2/9 years of >=7% EPS growth; no durable moat.

name: Stifel Financial Corp
reason: Wealth management plus institutional brokerage/IB whose earnings track capital-markets activity and interest on client cash; EPS at 1.0x 10y max (5.28) after a market-driven run, which fails the capital-markets-dependence test.

name: JPMorgan Chase & Co.
reason: Fortress-balance-sheet, scale-advantaged universal bank run by an exceptional manager (Dimon) with 12.8% 10y EPS CAGR, shares -2.9%/yr, negligible acquisitions and no loss year; caveat EPS at 1.0x 10y high (20.02) on elevated NII/credit and consensus FY2 only +3.3%, plus succession risk.

name: Insight Enterprises, Inc.
reason: Low-margin IT reseller (EBIT margin 5.1% at a 10y high, 100th pctile) whose EPS growth came largely from acquisitions (acq spend 1.02x FCF over 10y) with adjusted EPS 43% above GAAP and ND/EBITDA 2.4x; vendor/hyperscaler disintermediation risk.

name: Wintrust Financial Corporation
reason: Well-run, founder-built Chicago commercial bank with 14.6% 10y EPS CAGR and no loss year, but growth has been funded by share issuance (+2.7%/yr) and acquisitions (31% of FCF), EPS is at 1.0x its 10y max, and spread-driven specialty finance (premium finance) makes 10-year forecasting difficult.

name: First Citizens BancShares, Inc.
reason: Holding-family-controlled bank with superb capital allocation, but EPS more than doubled in 2023 on the SVB failed-bank deal and its bargain-purchase gain (adj EPS history only from 2020), so normalised earnings of the transformed franchise are not yet forecastable.

name: Upbound Group, Inc.
reason: Subprime rent-to-own/lease-to-own lender dependent on credit cycles and regulatory risk, with ND/EBITDA 3.6x, Acima acquisition spend 76% of FCF, rising shares and adjusted EPS several times GAAP (gap 536%).

name: McCormick & Company, Incorporated
reason: Durable branded spice franchise, but EPS grew only 5.6%/yr over 10y (1.2%/yr over 5y) with acquisition spend 90% of FCF, ND/EBITDA 3.1x and consensus FY2-FY3 4-9%; good business without a plausible route to >=7% EPS growth, plus GLP-1 volume risk.

name: Avient Corporation
reason: Portfolio-reshaped specialty polymer compounder whose 10y EPS CAGR is only 3.7% despite acquisition spend 2.07x FCF, 10y ROIC 5.0%, ND/EBITDA 3.2x and adjusted EPS 110% above GAAP; growth bought not organic.

name: Terex Corporation
reason: Cyclical construction/aerials equipment maker (EPS 0.13 in 2020 to 7.06 in 2023, now 4.93) with revenue -1.9%/yr over 10y, ND/EBITDA 3.1x after the Environmental Solutions acquisition (acq 1.15x FCF); earnings not forecastable.
